_why: The single declaration of which routes Cloudflare Access protects. Read by edge-visibility.test.ts, which fails when a route exists that is in neither list, and by scripts/check-access-boundary.sh, which verifies the live site matches. Adding a route to the app without classifying it here is a test failure rather than a silently public page.
_notPublicRoutes: This is NOT TokenGate's PUBLIC_ROUTES. That set is about in-app gating and includes /settings so a self-hoster can reach the connection screen. This set is the Cloudflare bypass list, and /settings is deliberately absent from it: it is reachable in-app without a session but must never be reachable from the internet without one.
_whenYouAddARoute: Add its top-level segment to protectedAtEdge here, AND add rhapto.augaster.com/<segment> to the destinations of the Cloudflare application that carries the Email Policy. The test catches the first omission; scripts/check-access-boundary.sh catches the second.
_publicAssets: Top-level directories of apps/web/public that a signed-out visitor must be able to fetch (the homepage video and poster). They are NOT App Router routes, so they are not in publicAtEdge. Under the live protected-prefix model they are public by default: Access covers only the prefixes in protectedAtEdge, so no Cloudflare change is needed. Never add one of these dirs to protectedAtEdge. scripts/check-access-boundary.sh probes each file for a 200 so a switch back to a hostname-wide application is caught.
